conflict_groups.label: Transformer MLP activation choice
conflict_groups.rationale: These patches replace the same baseline GELU path with incompatible activation or gated-MLP choices; after one promotion, the others must be reformulated as direct alternatives.

conflict_groups.label: Positional representation replacement
conflict_groups.rationale: Learned absolute positions and fixed ALiBi each remove baseline RoPE in different ways and cannot be applied together as written.

conflict_groups.label: RoPE geometry variants
conflict_groups.rationale: These proposals alter overlapping RoPE or relative-position code. A promoted member changes the baseline for every later member even when a combination remains conceptually possible.

conflict_groups.label: Core normalization formulation
conflict_groups.rationale: RMSNorm, fully affine LayerNorm, and a LayerNorm epsilon change target the same core normalization sites; later alternatives may become obsolete or require a new claim.

conflict_groups.label: Optimizer and training schedule
conflict_groups.rationale: Batch size, optimizer moments, clipping, regularization, warmup, learning rate, decay, and context curriculum jointly determine optimization; each result is conditional on earlier accepted recipe changes.

conflict_groups.label: Learning-rate curve
conflict_groups.rationale: These patches edit overlapping learning-rate defaults or schedule logic and must be adapted to any previously accepted curve change.

conflict_groups.label: Output parameterization and training objective
conflict_groups.rationale: Logit biases, scales, residual heads, and auxiliary losses alter the same output geometry or gradients, so later effect estimates depend on earlier accepted members.

conflict_groups.label: Attention topology and logits
conflict_groups.rationale: These patches share attention projections, masks, head layout, initialization, or positional logits. Accepted changes require code adaptation and a fresh interaction assessment.

conflict_groups.label: MLP structure and capacity
conflict_groups.rationale: These proposals alter MLP activation, width, placement, local mixing, or the architecture budget assigned to MLPs; they cannot be replayed blindly after a promotion.

conflict_groups.label: Residual layout and initialization
conflict_groups.rationale: These proposals modify residual branches, normalization, scale, initialization, or readout mixing and therefore share both code surfaces and optimization assumptions.

conflict_groups.label: Residual output initialization
conflict_groups.rationale: Projection biases, unscaled random initialization, and zero residual initialization are competing initialization formulations for the same output projections.

conflict_groups.label: Transformer block layout
conflict_groups.rationale: Depth-for-width, parallel branches, and sandwich MLPs change the block graph in ways that invalidate the other patches as direct fixed-parent alternatives.

conflict_groups.label: Document boundaries and local token mixing
conflict_groups.rationale: These proposals change which local or cross-story token relationships are modeled, so their gains may overlap and must be re-estimated after a related promotion.

conflict_groups.label: Auxiliary and masked training objectives
conflict_groups.rationale: Target masking, z-loss, two-token prediction, and midpoint supervision alter training gradients and must use mutually consistent ignored-token semantics.

conflict_groups.label: Embedding and tied-output parameterization
conflict_groups.rationale: These patches alter embedding scale, regularization, dimensionality, tied-output behavior, or embedding reinjection and require adaptation after any accepted member.

conflict_groups.label: One-million-parameter budget contention
conflict_groups.rationale: Each member consumes baseline parameter headroom. After one promotion, every later member must be re-budgeted against the 1,050,000-parameter cap.

objective: Screen all 60 unmeasured fixed-parent patches for lower held-out validation BPB while preserving protected integrity, resource, and parameter constraints.

principles: Queue rank is compute triage, not evidence that a patch is better.
Screen low-disruption and high-information hypotheses before parameter-heavy structural variants.
Place one representative from major conflict families early and defer redundant alternatives.
After every promotion, revalidate or adapt all remaining patches against the new accepted parent.
Never use queue order to select seeds, override protected outcomes, or claim model quality.
ranking_policy.tie_breaker: Prefer lower adaptation risk, then lower resource risk, then lower original proposal number; no measured outcome was used.
